title: 1964 AHSME Problem 9
statement: A jobber buys an article at \(\$24\) less \(12\dfrac12\%.\) He then wishes to sell the article at a gain of \(33\dfrac13\%\) of his cost after allowing a \(20\%\) discount on his marked price. At what price, in dollars, should the article be marked?

solutions.text:
The cost is \(24(1-\frac{1}{8})=21\) dollars. A gain of one third makes the desired selling price \(21(\frac{4}{3})=28\) dollars. If \(M\) is the marked price, then \(0.8M=28,\) so \(M=35.\) This is not listed.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Compute the discounted cost first, then increase it by one third
The selling price is \(80\%\) of the marked price
